contexts.text: The New Temple, (Ezekiel) = in general, a new Church, and a man of the Church, or one who is regenerate; for every regenerated one is a temple of the Lord. AC 4545:4.
He who is not a temple of the Lord, cannot be what is signified by the temple. which is the Church, and Heaven.
Before the temple was built, (the Jews) turned their faces to the east when they prayed.
Under Tabernacle, see this reference.

The New Jerusalem, and the New Temple = the Lord's Kingdom in the Heavens and on earth. ( = the Lord's Kingdom; in special, a new Church. AC 2830:5.) ( = in special, the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom; Zion, the Celestial one. AC 2830:5.) AC 3481:3. AC 3708:17. AC 9603:2.
The beginning of a new Church was represented by... the rebuilding of the temple.
Under Tent, see this reference.
Those frequent their synagogues; these their places of worship.
When man is called a house, there is signified the Celestial of faith with him; when a temple, the truth of faith with him. AC 3720.
They thought... that the temple was His footstool; not knowing that external representative worship was signified by the house of God, and the temple.
The images which are common in churches. HH 74:end. HH 340.
The altar was the principal representative of the Lord, and afterwards the temple.

(Thus) the temple = the Lord's Spiritual Church; in the universal sense, the Heaven of the spiritual Angels; in the most universal, the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom; and, in the supreme, the Lord as to Divine truth.
A temple = truth, because it was constructed of stones.
When a temple is mentioned there occurs to the Angels the idea of truth, and of such truth as is treated of in the series.
As the Israelites were prone to idolatry... they were gathered together to one place... where the temple was. Explained.
They had frequented churches where the Word is preached, but not to know the things of Heaven... AR 659:end. SE 2779:end. SE 5467:end. SE 5469. SE 5534. SE 5719. (See Frequent.)
When man becomes spiritual he no longer believes it holy to give... to places of worship which abound in wealth...
The temple of the Lord's body () = the Divine truth from the Divine good; for the temple = the Lord as to Divine truth; and Body, the Divine good... AE 220:2. AE 391:4. AE 706:11.
For the Stone, in general, = the temple; and, in special, its foundation; and the temple = the Lord's Divine Human. Illustrated.
Hence the temple at Jerusalem was built upon a mountain.
Everyone who lives in the good of charity and faith is a Church, and is a Kingdom of the Lord, and is hence called a temple, and also a house of God.
The New Temple = the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom. AC 8468:2. ( = the Spiritual Church. AC 7847:3) ( = the Heaven of the Lord. AC 8369:end.) ( = a new Spiritual Church from the Lord. AC 9050:10.)
The temple, in the supreme sense, = the Lord as to the Divine Human; and therefore, in the representative sense. His Church.
A life of piety consists in... frequenting churches, and in listening devoutly to the preaching there, etc.
For the temple = the Lord Himself; and, in the representative sense, Heaven.

The temple at Jerusalem was also built of whole stones (); for by the temple of the Lord was represented the Lord as to Divine truth. That the Lord was represented by the temple He Himself teaches in ; and that it was as to the Divine truth, was because it was taught there, and therefore also it was built of stones, (which) = Divine truth. AE 585:11.
The Jerusalem temple, whence were the vessels, in the supreme sense, = the Lord; in the representative sense, His Kingdom and Church. AC 9437:end.
The temple which sanctities the gold (). The temple represented the Lord Himself; and the gold. the good which is from Him. AE 391:5. AE 608:end.
The Lord shall suddenly come to His temple (). To the temple of the Lord = to His Human, as He Himself teaches... AC 10528:2. AE 242:9. AE 444:8.
As by a temple is signified Heaven or the Church, it has been customary from ancient times to give to places of worship a situation towards the east and the west. Explained. DLW 123.

There were two things by which the Lord as to the Divine Human was represented: the temple, and the altar. Illustrated... But the temple was a representative of the Lord as to His Divine truth, thus as to Heaven; for the Divine truth proceeding from Him makes Heaven; and it is therefore said of the temple, that he who shall swear by the temple, will swear by it and by Him who dwelleth in it... AE 391:3. AE 915.
The temple of God, and the altar () = Heaven and the Church; the temple = the Spiritual Church; and the altar, the Celestial Church.
When anyone is in a temple that he is not at home... they say that he is not at home...
The Lord called Himself the temple... because the temple represented His Divine Human. DSS 47.
In the Heavens... there are temples... in which there is preaching.

It has been granted me to enter their temples, and hear the preaching. The preacher stands in a pulpit on the east; before his face sit those who are in the light of wisdom... They sit in the form of a circus, so that all are in view of the preacher... At the entrance, which is at the east of the temple, and on the left of the pulpit, stand those who are being initiated. No one is allowed to stand behind the pulpit... The temples appear as of stone in the Spiritual Kingdom; and as of wood in the Celestial... The latter are not called temples, but houses of God; and are devoid of magnificence; but in the Spiritual Kingdom they have magnificence greater or less.
They who have lived... continually in churches...

In His temple everyone saith. Glory () = that in every particular of the Word there are Divine truths; for the temple = the Lord, and thence the Word, and also Heaven and the Church; and glory = the Divine truth.

That by the externals of the Jerusalem temple were represented the externals of the Word... is because by the temple, as by the tabernacle, was represented Heaven and the Church, and thence also the Word. Explained.
Spirits who heard the singing of a Psalm in a place of worship on Earth. DeVerbo 18:2.
Man endows places of worship... and attends them sedulously... and does not know whether he does so from himself, or from God. Explained.
Like one who sees a magnificent temple...
Why it was granted to Solomon to build the temple, by which was signified the Divine Human of the Lord (), and also the Church.
Why many kings after Solomon were permitted to profane the temple.
The devastation itself of the Church was represented by the destruction of the temple itself...
They placed such images in their temples, to call to remembrance the holy things they signified.
The consummation of the Israelitish and Jewish Church is meant by the destruction of the Jerusalem temple... and, finally, by the second destruction of the temple...
In the temples there, no one can sit anywhere but in his own place...

I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God () = that truths from good... support the Lord's Church in Heaven. A temple = the Church; and the temple of My God, the Lord's Church in Heaven. AE 219.

A temple, in the supreme sense, = the Lord as to the Divine Human; in special, as to the Divine truth. But in the representative sense, temple = the Lord's Church in Heaven, and also the Lord's Church in the world. Illustrated.
The temple () = the present Church; and its dissolution so that there should not be one stone upon another = the end of this Church, in that there would not be any truth left...

The temple = these three things: the Lord, the Church in Heaven, and the Church in the world; because these three make a one, and cannot be separated, consequently the one cannot be meant without the other. AR 529.
They serve Him day and night in His temple () = that they live according to truths... in His Church. ( = that they are constantly kept in truths in Heaven. AE 478. AE 478:3, Explained.)
Arise, and measure the temple of God... () = to see and Know the state of the Church in the New Heaven... The temple = the Church as to the truth of doctrine. AE 629.
The temple = the Church as to its internal; the courts, as to its external.

The temple of God was opened in Heaven () = the New Heaven in which the Lord is worshipped in His Divine Human... The temple of God, here, = the Lord in His Divine Human in Heaven. ( = the appearing of a New Heaven and a New Church, where there is the worship of the Lord. AE 699.)
Tabernacle = the Celestial Church; temple, the Spiritual Church. (See Tabernacle.)
The temple = Heaven as to the Church; for there is a Church there too.

Another Angel went out of the temple which is in Heaven () = the Heavens of the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom. Explained. ( = manifestation by the Lord concerning the devastation of the Church as to Divine truth such as it is in Heaven. AE 914.)
Under Tabernacle, see this reference.
The temple, in the supreme sense, = the Lord as to His Divine Human, and thence Heaven and the Church; here, the Christian Heaven.
The temple () = the inmost of Heaven, where are the Word and the decalogue.

The temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power () = the inmost of Heaven full of Divine truth spiritual and celestial from the Lord. ( = Divine truth, or the Word, in the natural sense, in light and power from Divine truth in the spiritual sense. AE 955.)
I heard a great voice out of the temple () = an influx from the Lord from the inmost of Heaven. ( = the Divine truth from the Word. AE 959.)
A great voice came out of the temple of Heaven () = a manifestation by the Lord from the inmost of Heaven. AE 1013.
The temple of Wisdom, seen and described. CL 56, revisited. TCR 387.

I saw no temple in it; for the Lord God Almighty is the temple of it, and the Lamb () = that in this Church there will be no external separated from ah internal, because the Lord Himself in His Divine Human, from whom is everything of the Church, is alone approached, worshipped, and adored. I saw no temple in it does not mean that in the New Church... there will be no places of worship... AE 699:end.
For a temple = the Church as to worship; and, in the supreme sense, the Lord as to His Divine Human, who is to be worshipped...
Under Tabernacle, see this reference.
There was seen a magnificent palace, and in its inmost a temple (within which was held a Council of the clergy). Described. BE 120. TCR 188.
He introduced them into a little city, in the middle of which was a temple, (where people were engaged in an unceasing worship of God). Described.

The Angel said. The worship of God... is performed in our temples, and lasts about two hours. (They entered, and found that) it was a large temple, capable of holding about three thousand persons. It was a semi-rotunda, the benches or seats being continuous in a circular sweep according to the figure of the temple; and the back seats were raised higher than the front ones. The pulpit in front of the seats was drawn back a little from the centre; the door was behind the pulpit, on the left... Everyone who enters the temple knows his own place... and cannot sit anywhere else. If he does so, he hears and [perceives nothing, and disturbs the order, in which case the priest is not inspired. (The service described. CL 24.)
(In the Heaven of the Silver Age) we saw temples of precious stones of a sapphire and azure colour.
Priests pray in the churches that...
(So) a temple must first be built... then inaugurated, and finally prayer offered that God may be present and unite Himself with the Church there.

I once entered a temple in the World of Spirits... and, before the sermon, they reasoned together about Redemption. The temple was square, without windows in the walls, but had a large opening in the middle of the roof...
Windows were then made in the temple at the sides, through which light inflowed from the four quarters...
Those of Babel, when they enter the church...
So they destroyed the temple built by the Lord through the apostles, until not one stone was left upon another... by which temple is meant not only the Jerusalem temple, but also the Church.
I saw multitudes (of the boreal Spirits) flocking to a temple, which was buried out of sight in snow. (The interior, and the service of the temple described.)
The temple represented the Heaven in which are the spiritual Angels; the tabernacle, that in which are the celestial Angels...

Illustrated by comparison with a temple. Man, according to Paul, is a temple of God (. ; ). As a temple of God, man has salvation and eternal life as his end... In this way man becomes a temple of God.
They were assembled (to deliberate on free will) in a certain round temple, like the temple in Rome called the Pantheon. (The interior described.)

One day there appeared a magnificent temple, square in form, the roof of which was crown-shaped... Its walls were continuous windows of crystal, its gate of pearl. Within, on the south side near the west, was a pulpit, on which at the right lay the open Word... In the centre of the temple was a shrine... where stood a cherub of gold... This temple signified the New Church. (The correspondences in it explained.) I saw this writing above the gate, Nunc Licet.
Or sleep at night in a temple, beneath the floor of which are graves...
The instructive and oratorical preaching in temples...
The uses of the two sacraments compared to a temple buried in the ground...
These sacraments may also be compared to a double temple. Described.
The temples in that Earth constructed of living trees. Described.
The Dutch do not tolerate images and pictures in their churches...
When I entered St. Paul's Cathedral...
The Lord is thus pictured in their churches.
Dream of an overthrown and ruined temple, which represented the present state of the Church.
Temples of plastered stone seen in the north.
On the temples (of the solifidians), and how they sit. Described. SE 4936. SE 4938.
St. Peter's Cathedral in Rome, mentioned.
While they are reading these prayers in the churches...

On the temples and preachings. - In the temples everyone knows his own place... by influx from the Lord... All taken together form as it were one man. Described. Anyone outside the temple who hears, and looks into the congregation, causes all their thoughts to be varied. Explained. SE 6056:end.
Hence it was evident that the Lord disposes all in the temples (there) through Angels and Spirits above or outside of them, according to the nature of the hearers. Explained.
On Jerusalem, and the temple, after the captivity. (The dates given.)
The New Temple,etc. = a New Church. AE 422:8.
Temple = the Lord as to Divine truth. AE 329:29.
The temple of God, in the supreme, = the Lord's Divine Human; in the relative, His Spiritual Kingdom, thus the Heaven which constitutes it.
As the temple = Heaven, it follows that all things of the temple = such things as are of Divine truth. AE 219:5.

Temple, in the Word, = the Lord's Divine Human; in the relative sense. Heaven; and therefore also the Church... and therefore also the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord. Fully illustrated, seriatim.
To carry into their temples () = to turn into profane worship.
The temple = Heaven and the Church...
Temple = a Church which is in truths from good, which is called a Spiritual Church. AE 799:6.
To defile the temple of holiness () = to profane worship.
Temple = the worship which proceeds from truths from good. AE 391:19.
The house of prayer, that is, the temple, = the Heaven where spiritual truths are, thus also spiritual truths such as are there.
This is said of the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem, and by the new temple there is signified a new Church which was to be instaurated by the Lord. Described.
For the temple of Solomon was destroyed before the captivity, and a new one was built when they returned. By temple is signified Divine worship; and by a new temple, worship restored.
Why the temple (in Ezekiel) was measured according to the quarters.
Therefore the ancients built their temples so that the front parts, where the adytum was, should look to the east; which, from the old custom, is still done.
The temple = the Lord's Divine Human.
The New Temple = the New Church to be instaurated by the Lord when He came into the world.
Temple = Heaven where truths reign.
Jehovah is in the temple of His holiness () = Heaven, where and whence is Divine truth.

To swear by the temple = to swear by the Lord, Heaven, and the Church; for by temple... is meant the Lord as to Divine truth, ... Heaven and the Church as to Divine truth, and also all worship from Divine truth.
Temple, in the Word, = the Church as to truth, because it was of stones; house of God = the Church as to good, because in ancient times it was of wood.

The temple, regarded in itself, = the higher Heavens; namely, the adytum, where was the ark, = the Third Heaven; the temple outside the adytum, the Middle Heaven; and hence the court, the First Heaven. And that which = Heaven, also = the Church... and that which = the Church, also = the Word, and likewise worship. Explained. AE 630:6. AE 630:8. AE 700:33.
That the temple = the Church. Illustrated.
We shall be satisfied with... the holiness of Thy temple () = to be in intelligence from Divine truth, and to enjoy heavenly joy from it.
The temple = Heaven and the Church as to Divine truth.
Solomon therefore built three houses: the house of God, or the temple, for the Spiritual...
The new Church to be instaurated by the Lord... is signified by... the temple ().
The temple = the Church as to truth.
Under Tent, see this reference.
The temples in which are dragons () = the goods and truths of the Word and of the Church, which are adulterated and profaned.
Afterwards the temple was built, in which also all things were representative. Enumerated.
Therefore there are intermediate Angels... who preach and teach truths in the temples (of the celestial Angels), which are called houses of God, and are of wood.
The temple = Heaven and the Church, and the Divine which proceeds from the Lord.
In the temple the Word was taught... Thus the temple represented the Lord as to Divine truth.
The temple = Divine truth from the Lord.
The temple = the interior Word revealed.
The temple = Heaven as to Divine truth.
As wood = good, therefore with the Most Ancients, who were in the good of love, the temples ere of wood: which were not called temples, but houses of God.
As soon as these preach, all go out, and the church becomes empty.
The preachers proceed... in this way to the middle of the city (London) to the places of worship.
